comment: Parity of the personal launchers with pose delegate (spec pose-delegation-parity-gate). One row per capability the ADR's 'Retirement by parity' section enumerates, in its words; each names the native command that replaces it and the tests that cover it. The check in pose-mcp/internal/cli/launcher_parity_test.go fails while any row has no command or test, names a test or a command flag that does not exist, or the ADR enumerates a capability no row carries.

rows.capability: lead detection and opposite vendor, `--lead`, `--target`
same-vendor warning
`--read-only`, `--sandboxed`, `--full-access`, `--no-network`
write mode with the vendor's automatic approver
rows.note: The approver is part of the agent's write command in .pose/policy/delegation.json, as it was part of the launcher's write invocation; the test runs an approving agent through it.

rows.capability: `--cd`, `--add-dir`, `--effort`, models by configuration
rows.note: Models are configured per agent in .pose/policy/delegation.json.

rows.capability: running outside a Git repository
`--resume` from a run or a raw session, reusing its settings, with a default continuation message
rows.note: A raw session, one POSE never recorded, continues with pose delegate task --session; a run POSE recorded continues with pose delegate resume <run> [--prompt <file|->], reusing its agent, access and settings. Both send the default continuation message without a prompt.

rows.capability: usage-limit detection with the resume hint
`--label`
`--dry-run`
prompt, events, final message, stderr, command, session and exit code kept per run
final message on stdout and the agent's exit code
removal of the parent's session variables
list with state, turns, age and last step
selection by label, run name or session prefix
picker with live preview and refresh
follow that stops on exit, and no-follow
verbose output tail with a line bound
resumed chains replayed with a marker at each hand-over
both vendors' event formats
`NO_COLOR` and no colour off a terminal
rows.note: watch takes the output profile every command takes; NO_COLOR is resolved there.
